correctness.rationale: For a zero on the independent side, Italian domination depends only on the clique weight \(c\). Defending such a zero lowers c by one and removes one independent zero, giving exactly the thresholds \(c\ge2\) for \(q=1\) and \(c\ge3\) for \(q\ge2\). When \(q=0\), every independent vertex is positive; the only insecure all-zero-clique labeling is the one with all independent labels equal to 1. The three disjoint profile classes yield the displayed generating function by direct counting. The bundled verifier independently checks the definition, criterion, coefficients, and minimum on 28 complete split types and 191916 ternary labelings through order nine.

value.rationale: The primary paper already resolves the optimization value on this dense family, making a mere repetition of the minimum routine. The final claim instead classifies every secure Italian function and gives the full weight distribution. This is a natural strengthening of an explicitly studied parameter on an explicitly studied join family and supports coefficient, random-labeling, and enumeration questions unavailable from the minimum alone.
